newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil gov't to sell Petrobras shares in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Brazil gov't to sell Petrobras shares in 1997.

text.p: Brazil's federal government plans to sell more than one third of the voting share capital it detains in state oil monopoly Petrobras in 1997, Planning Minister Antonio Kandir said.
The government currently holds 82 percent of Petrobras' voting share capital, equivalent to 51 percent of total capital.

Petrobras President Joel Mendes Renno said Friday the constitutional amendment opening up the Brazilian oil sector to competition included plans to reduce the government holding in Petrobras to 50 percent of voting share capital plus one share.
Kandir confirmed the government's intention to reduce its stake in Petrobras next year once Congress has passed legislation regulating the break-up of the state oil monopoly.
The funds resulting from the sale of the Petrobras shares will go towards paying off government debt, according to Kandir, who spoke at a lunch at the American Chamber of Commerce in Rio de Janeiro.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
